brief.headline: Push for ₹32.69 L/yr saving to match best price we already pay, plus faster cash by paying sooner for a price cut

priceAsk.summary: Ask them to match ₹290.00/KG (the lowest price we pay Shrinath Roto Pack) on our top three ORS laminate SKUs
priceAsk.target: ₹32.69 L/yr saving by closing the gap to ₹290.00/KG
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹290.00/KG to Shrinath Roto Pack for the same type of laminate — their ₹294.03–308.30/KG is 1.4–6.3% higher. The market ask band is ₹205–305/kg, so ₹290 sits comfortably inside fair range and we know it's real because we pay it today.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Offer to pay them 15 days faster (cut our 30 Days After Receipt to 15) in exchange for a price cut of roughly 4.38%
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Paying 15 days faster frees up ₹1.16 Cr of our cash, but their borrowing rate is 4.38% (ranging 1.55-9.25%), so every rupee we pay early is worth about that rate to them — trade the early cash for a matching price cut

brief.financialLeverage: They keep only 1.1% of every ₹100 they sell as profit (similar firms keep 2.1%), so there's little room to squeeze on price alone. But their cash is stuck for 81 days versus 46 days at similar firms, meaning cash is tight for them and they'll value faster payment. We're 9.72% of their ₹291.36 Cr revenue — a big enough customer to ask for better terms without risking our supply. Their rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable, but the agency notes they stopped cooperating, so treat their health as uncertain and keep a second source lined up.

evidence.point: We pay ₹32.69 L/yr more than the best price we already get
Best price we pay is ₹290.00/KG (Shrinath Roto Pack); GEEP charges ₹294.03–308.30/KG
Market asking price for pharma ORS laminate is ₹205–305/kg, typical ₹250/kg — our target ₹290 is inside that fair band
We are 9.72% of their total sales (₹28.31 Cr out of ₹291.36 Cr)
Their cash is stuck for 81 days; similar firms tie up cash for only 46 days
They borrow money at rates between 1.55-9.25%, effective 4.38% — paying them early is worth about that rate

alternates.name: Huhtamaki India Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexible-packaging converter already supplying FDC in small volumes — a proven, scalable second source for laminate sachets (health C 58/100, revenue ₹2755.75 Cr)

alternates.name: UFLEX Ltd
alternates.why: Listed flexibles giant that makes both film and converts it — can replace GEEP at scale (health C 46/100, revenue ₹16492.00 Cr)

alternates.name: Constantia Parikh Packaging Pvt Ltd
alternates.why: Part of global Constantia group, does pharma blister and sachet laminates in India — strong second-source candidate (health D 31/100, revenue ₹222.04 Cr)

risks: GEEP is 76% of our Laminates spend (₹28.31 Cr) — we have almost no backup today, so qualify Huhtamaki or UFLEX fast before pushing too hard
Their rating is CRISIL BB+ / Stable but the agency says 'issuer not cooperating' — their real health may be shakier than the rating suggests, so watch for supply hiccups
They keep only 1.1% profit on every sale versus 2.1% at peer firms — a big price cut could squeeze them into trouble; focus the win on payment terms and the smaller ₹32.69 L price gap
Risk flags include GST filing delays, EPF payment delays, and pending legal cases — monitor delivery and quality closely through the contract period
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We value the partnership, and to keep growing our ₹28.31 Cr business with you we need two things: match the ₹290/KG we already pay elsewhere, and let's talk about paying you faster in exchange for a rate cut that helps us both.
